verdicts.summary: The new guard in dispatchSteerIntoRun rejects a steer into a run with a persisted interrupt request. The failed command commits nothing, so the queued run stays queued and held.
verdicts.scenario: Tried to break it two ways. (1) Promote-to-steer after Stop: the handler emits cancel events for the queued run (7770-7809) before calling dispatchSteerIntoRun, and the guard then throws. Those events are only returned to the caller on success (11244), so an error discards them and the queued run is not cancelled. (2) A run that legitimately keeps running after an interrupt request would be steer-locked forever. The request item is written only by Stop commands (9589-9598 and the no-session branch at 9550). The restart-steering path (4189 onward) never writes one, so a restarted attempt is not locked out.

verdicts.summary: The downgrade to queue_after_active lands in a working queue path. The stopped run still counts as blocking, the hold is released for user sends, and the new run is created without queueHeld.
verdicts.scenario:
Tried plain auto sends in the Stop window, from a user client and from a non-user sender. Also tried a stopped run in waiting status and a send carrying a notification.
- resolveDeliveryIntent only picks runs in preparing, starting, running or waiting (CommandPolicy.ts:154-160). isBlockingRun accepts the same four statuses (Orchestrator.ts:525-531), so shouldQueue is true at 5026 and the message queues behind the stopped run instead of starting concurrently.
- A user client send releases held runs (5046-5063). The new run gets queueHeld only when nothing was released (5173-5178).
- A non-user sender releases nothing, so the new run is created held because a held queued run exists.
- A notification with deliveryIntent auto now passes the check at 4827-4836 where it previously errored as a steer. This is a benign change.
The delegated-completion override at 4886-4919 can still turn the downgraded mode back into a steer. Finding 0 already covers that.
